title: Use `pd.read_csv()` to read a spreadsheet file into a DataFrame, and use `head()` to view the first few rows.
body: In pandas, `pd.read_csv()` reads a CSV file into a DataFrame. `df.head()` is used to quickly check the first few rows to see if the data was read correctly.
detail: Immediately after reading a file, it’s a good idea to check whether the rows and columns are as expected, rather than processing the entire dataset right away. By looking at `df.head()`, `df.shape`, and `df.columns` together, you can quickly check the file structure and easily identify issues such as incorrect delimiters or column names early on. For beginners, it’s safest to first check the first five rows and the column names before moving on to filtering or calculations.

title: df['column_name'] selects a column, and the condition filters the rows
body: In pandas, `df['score']` selects the single `score` column. If you write it as `df[df['score'] >= 80]`, it keeps only the rows that satisfy the condition, so you must first verify that the column name is correct.
detail: The part that confuses beginners the most is the difference between column selection and row filtering. df['score'] is an expression that retrieves a column, while df['score'] >= 80 creates a True/False condition. When that condition is placed inside df[...], rows are filtered. In other words, you need to distinguish between the step of selecting a column and the step of retaining rows based on a condition.

title: df.to_csv(..., index=False) removes unnecessary index columns
body: index=False omits DataFrame row labels from the CSV. That avoids an unnecessary column for a disposable RangeIndex, but a meaningful identifier stored in the index must not be discarded. Confirm its meaning and read the output back to verify the columns.

title: NaN is a missing value and is handled using isna, fillna, or dropna.
body: NaN or NA is a pandas missing-value marker and may not be the same as an empty string. After counting missing entries with isna().sum(), choose deletion or imputation based on data meaning. A zero score and an unrecorded score are different, so record the rule and affected rows.
